name: Manage requests for information
summary: A request for information (RFI) is a written question from the contractor to the design consultant when drawings or specifications are unclear, conflict or do not fit site conditions. The field engineer researches and drafts it, the assistant project manager reviews, logs and chases it, the consultant answers, and the project manager decides whether the answer changes scope. Late answers stop or re-sequence work, some answers are never given formally, and about one in five or six answers turns into a change notice.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor of about 2,800 employees building institutional, commercial and industrial buildings, with about 220 active projects run from regional offices, a web-based project management platform and a construction ERP.
baseline.notes: Practice described for Ontario stipulated-price and construction-management projects on CCDC contract forms; Western and Atlantic projects follow the same pattern under their provincial lien and safety laws.

unit_of_work: one RFI (one question raised by a trade or the site team)
trigger: A subcontractor, the superintendent's walk or BIM coordination raises a question the documents do not answer.
end_state: The answer is distributed, the field set is updated and the RFI is closed, or the question is closed without an RFI or without a formal answer.

volume.seasonality: RFIs come mostly in the first half of each project, during structure and mechanical-electrical rough-in, so company volume follows new project starts more than the calendar; a little higher from April to October.

evidence.note: Navigant: 17.2 RFIs per $1 million of construction cost on $5M-$50M projects (src ascc). At about $1.5 billion of annual construction revenue this gives about 2,150 RFIs a month; low and high allow for revenue of $1.2B to $2.0B and for institutional work, which tends to run higher. The organisation file's 3,300 a month (15 per project per month) is above this.
Share of the role's time on RFIs, author's estimate; headcount from the organisation file. 120 field engineers x about 0.22.
Share of the role's time on RFIs, author's estimate; headcount from the organisation file. 140 assistant project managers x about 0.10.
Share of the role's time on RFIs, author's estimate; headcount from the organisation file. 110 project managers x about 0.05.
Share of the role's time on RFIs, author's estimate; headcount from the organisation file. 120 superintendents x about 0.02.

systems.name: Project management platform (drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, change events)
BIM and clash detection tools (Revit, Navisworks)
CPM scheduling software (Primavera P6, Microsoft Project)
Construction ERP (job cost, general ledger, payables, receivables, payroll)

steps.name: Receive the question from a trade or the field
steps.description: The field engineer receives a question from a subcontractor by email, phone or the project platform, or from the superintendent's walk, and reads it to see whether it is a real question about the design or a request for direction that the site team can give.

error.defect_description: A question about scope is treated as a simple field question.

evidence.note: Questions wait up to a day for the field engineer, who is also doing layout and site checks; author's estimate.

steps.name: Search the documents for an existing answer
steps.description: The field engineer searches the current drawings, specifications, addenda, earlier RFI answers and reviewed shop drawings for an answer, and checks whether a revised drawing has already resolved the conflict.

error.defect_description: An existing answer is missed and a duplicate RFI is issued.

evidence.note: FMI/PlanGrid: 5.5 hours a week per person looking for project data such as revised drawings; the 15% resolved without an RFI is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Reply to the trade with the document reference
steps.description: The field engineer replies to the trade or superintendent with the drawing, detail or specification clause that answers the question, attaches a marked-up snip, and closes the question without issuing an RFI.

error.defect_description: The reference is wrong and the trade builds to it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Investigate the condition in the field
steps.description: The field engineer goes to the location, measures the conflict, checks what is already installed, photographs it and talks to the trade foreman so the RFI states the actual condition and a workable proposed solution.

error.defect_description: A dimension is mis-measured.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; most RFIs on building projects concern a dimensional or coordination conflict that needs a field check.

steps.name: Draft the RFI with a proposed solution
steps.description: The field engineer writes the RFI in the project platform: the question, drawing and specification references, photos or a sketch, a proposed solution, whether cost or schedule may be affected, and the date an answer is needed to avoid delay.

error.defect_description: Question is ambiguous or lacks references, inviting a request for clarification.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the GC's own share of the about 8 hours of review and response per RFI reported by Navigant (src ascc) is taken as 2 to 4 hours, the rest falling on the design team.

steps.name: Review the RFI before issue
steps.description: The assistant project manager reads the draft for clarity, checks it is not a duplicate, removes wording that would concede scope, confirms the required-by date against the lookahead, and either returns it or passes it on.

error.defect_description: A scope-conceding phrase is left in.

control.basis: Company project procedure: RFIs reviewed by the project office before issue to the consultant

evidence.note: Author's estimate of review practice and return rate.

steps.name: Decide on a work-around while the answer is pending
steps.description: The superintendent looks at the affected area and the lookahead and decides whether crews can work elsewhere, whether to proceed at risk with the proposed solution, or whether work stops until the answer arrives, and tells the trade.

error.defect_description: Work proceeds at risk and must be redone when the answer differs.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; a quarter of RFIs flagged as schedule-critical.

steps.name: Log the RFI and set the due date
steps.description: The assistant project manager numbers the RFI, assigns the consultant reviewer and any sub-consultant, sets the contractual or agreed response date, and adds it to the RFI log shown at the weekly consultant meeting.

error.defect_description: Wrong reviewer is assigned and the RFI sits unread.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Send the RFI to the consultant
steps.description: The project platform emails the RFI to the consultant's contract administrator with the attachments and due date, records the date sent, and starts the overdue clock shown in the RFI log.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Automatic notification in the project platform; where the consultant insists on its own system the assistant project manager re-keys the RFI (not modelled).

steps.name: Consultant reviews and answers
steps.description: The architect's contract administrator reviews the RFI, routes it to the structural, mechanical or electrical sub-consultant where needed, and returns a written answer, a sketch, a supplemental instruction, or a request for more information.

error.defect_description: Answer is incomplete or conflicts with another discipline.

evidence.note: Navigant study: average response just below 10 days (src cj); wait range set so the mean answer time including chases is about 10 days. The consultant's own review hours (most of Navigant's about 8 hours per RFI, src ascc) are outside the organisation and not counted as touch time.

steps.name: Chase the overdue RFI
steps.description: The assistant project manager emails and phones the consultant about overdue RFIs, raises them at the weekly consultant meeting with the required-by dates, and records the delay so it can support a later time extension.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Weekly meeting cadence; author's estimate.

steps.name: Consultant answers after the chase
steps.description: After the reminder the consultant either sends the written answer, answers verbally at the meeting or by issuing a revised drawing or supplemental instruction that supersedes the RFI, or still leaves it outstanding.

error.defect_description: A verbal answer is not confirmed in writing.

next.condition: answered at the meeting or superseded by a revised drawing

evidence.note: Navigant found roughly 22% of RFIs never formally answered (src cj); here 0.28 x 0.35 plus repeat chases gives about 11% closed without a formal answer, as GCs close many unanswered RFIs once a revised drawing covers them. Branch shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the answer
steps.description: The field engineer reads the answer against the question and the field condition, checks that every discipline's comments agree and that it can be built, and returns it as a follow-up RFI if it is incomplete.

error.defect_description: An answer that conflicts with another trade's work is accepted.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of follow-up rate.

steps.name: Assess cost and schedule impact
steps.description: The project manager reads the answer against the contract scope and the subcontract scopes, and decides whether it changes the work, the cost or the schedule enough to give notice of a change to the consultant and owner.

error.defect_description: A scope change is not recognised and its cost is absorbed.

next.condition: answer changes scope, cost or time

evidence.note: About one RFI in five to six leads to a change notice; author's estimate from practice, not from a source opened.

steps.name: Give notice of a change
steps.description: The project manager writes a change notice or request for a change quotation citing the RFI answer, asks affected trades for pricing, and records it in the change log so the change order process can price and negotiate it.

error.defect_description: Notice misses the contract notice period.

control.basis: CCDC 2 Part 6: written notice of changes and claims within the contract periods

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Distribute the answer to trades
steps.description: The assistant project manager forwards the answer through the platform to every affected subcontractor and the superintendent, asks for pricing where it is a change, and marks the RFI as answered in the log.

error.defect_description: A trade affected by the answer is not copied.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Update the field drawing set
steps.description: The field engineer links or clouds the RFI answer on the current drawings in the platform and on the paper set in the trailer, and notes it for the as-built record so crews build to the answer.

error.defect_description: The paper set in the trailer is not updated and a crew builds to the old detail.

evidence.note: Poor project information accounts for 22% of rework (src cdive); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Brief the field crews
steps.description: The superintendent tells the affected foremen about the answer at the next start-up meeting or at the work face and confirms any work-around or stopped work can now proceed.

error.defect_description: A foreman is not told.

evidence.note: Next morning start-up meeting; author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the RFI in the log
steps.description: The assistant project manager records the answer date and the linked change notice, if any, and closes the RFI so the log shows response times and open items for the monthly report and any later claim.

error.defect_description: RFI left open in the log.

evidence.note: Logs are tidied weekly before the consultant meeting; author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the RFI as superseded or answered at the meeting
steps.description: The assistant project manager records the meeting minute or revised drawing that answered the RFI, asks the consultant to confirm in writing where the answer was verbal, and either closes the RFI or sends it for impact review.

error.defect_description: A verbal answer is never confirmed and later disputed.

next.condition: closed without a formal written answer

evidence.note: Reflects Navigant's finding that about 22% of RFIs never receive a formal answer (src cj); split is the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Overdue answer chased
exceptions.description: The consultant misses the due date; the assistant project manager chases weekly until a written answer, a revised drawing or a verbal answer arrives.

exceptions.name: Closed without a formal answer
exceptions.description: The question is answered at a meeting or overtaken by a revised drawing and closed without a written RFI response.

exceptions.name: Answer changes scope
exceptions.description: The project manager gives notice of a change and the answer feeds the change order process.

exceptions.name: Follow-up RFI
exceptions.description: The consultant asks for more information or the answer is incomplete, so the RFI is redrafted and re-issued.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from question raised to RFI closed

evidence.note: Built from the Navigant mean consultant response of just under 10 days (src cj) plus one to three days of GC drafting, review and distribution; the p90 reflects RFIs that are chased for several weeks.

benchmarks.population: Over 1 million RFIs on over 1,300 projects of $5M to $5B

evidence.note: Reported as 'just below 10 days'; 9.7 is the figure commonly quoted for the Navigant study.

pain_points.description: Consultant answers average about ten days and some never come, so crews work around open questions or proceed at risk.

evidence.note: Navigant: average response just under 10 days, about 22% never answered.

pain_points.description: Many questions are already answered in the documents or earlier RFIs, but finding the current information takes hours.

evidence.note: 5.5 hours a week per person looking for project data.

pain_points.description: Scope-changing answers are not always recognised, so the cost is absorbed instead of claimed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from practice.

pain_points.description: Paper drawing sets in the trailer fall out of step with RFI answers, a source of rework.

evidence.note: Poor project information causes 22% of rework.

sources.title: Request for Information (RFI) and Rework
sources.publisher: American Society of Concrete Contractors, The Voice newsletter (Bruce Suprenant)
sources.supports: Summary of the Navigant Construction Forum study 'Impact & Control of RFIs on Construction Projects': 1,362 projects, an average of about 800 RFIs per project, about 8 hours on average to review and respond to an RFI, $1,080 average cost per RFI, 17.2 RFIs per $1 million of construction cost on $5M-$50M projects and 1.1 on $1B-$5B projects.

sources.title: The cost of RFIs and best practices for construction professionals
sources.supports: Summary of the Navigant Construction Forum RFI study (Hughes, Wells, Nutter, Zack): over 1 million RFIs on over 1,300 projects of $5 million to $5 billion; average response time just below 10 days; roughly 22% of RFIs never answered; slightly more than $1,000 per RFI in administrative and technical review.

sources.title: Industry could be overspending $177B per year, study finds
sources.supports: FMI and PlanGrid 'Construction Disconnected' survey of 600 professionals (49% general contractors): 35% of time on non-optimal activities, more than 14 hours per person per week; 5.5 hours a week looking for project data, almost 5 hours managing disagreements, nearly 4 hours on mistakes needing rework; poor communication 26% and poor project information 22% of rework.

assumptions: The simulated median of about 13.5 days is above the 11-day benchmark because the company-side queues (field engineer, assistant project manager and project manager) are tier C estimates that add about three days to the Navigant consultant response; the consultant step alone reproduces a mean answer time of about 10 days.
Volume is set from the Navigant rate of 17.2 RFIs per $1 million of construction cost (src ascc) applied to about $1.5 billion of revenue, not from the organisation file's 3,300 a month.
The 15% of questions resolved from the documents without a formal RFI are counted as cases, because the field engineer still does the intake and search.

Consultant and sub-consultant review time is outside the organisation and is given zero touch time, so the staffing check covers company staff only; Navigant's about 8 hours per RFI (src ascc) covers all parties.
The interface to ops-change-order is attached to the 'answered' outcome; about 15% of answered RFIs produce a change request.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (1.35 loading factor for salaried staff).
US-heavy Navigant figures are used as a proxy for Canadian practice, as CCDC contracts and consultant practice are similar.
